tool: Antigravity CLI (agy) 1.5.15 in print mode, run in an empty directory outside the repository: `agy -p "<request>" --model gemini-4-neon-high --mode accept-edits --sandbox --output-format json`. The agent hands the request to its built-in image-generator subagent, which writes the image prompt and calls its generate_image tool.
model: gemini-3.1-flash-image behind generate_image (the service named it in a capacity error of the same session; the tool does not report it on success); agent gemini-4-neon-high; image-generator subagent gemini-4-hydrogen-tiered-high.
prompt: A seamless tileable PBR albedo surface texture of a powder-coated painted steel sheet. Very light, near-neutral grey paint (#D8DADB to #E0E2E3) featuring a fine, uniform orange-peel powder-coat micro-texture across the entire frame, with only a few very faint tiny hairline scratches and subtle minimal specks of dust. Viewed perfectly straight on (orthographic top-down flat macro photography), completely flat and even diffuse lighting across the whole surface, no directional light, no shadows, no bright specular highlights, no vignetting, no borders, no perspective distortion, no objects, no text, no logos, no markings. Uniform scale and density of orange-peel grain from edge to edge so it tiles seamlessly in a 3D material, photorealistic, high-resolution, square 1:1.
request: Generate exactly one image with aspect ratio 1:1 and nothing else. Image description: A seamless tileable surface texture of powder-coated painted steel sheet: a very light, near-neutral grey paint with a fine orange-peel micro texture and only a few faint tiny scratches and specks of dust, viewed perfectly straight on (orthographic, top-down), completely flat even diffuse lighting, no shadows, no specular highlights, no vignetting, no perspective, no objects, no text, no logos, no markings, uniform detail across the whole frame so it can tile seamlessly in a 3D material, photorealistic, square.
postProcessing: 1. ImageMagick 7.1.2-36, a one-off conversion of the generated JPEG to an 8-bit RGB PNG: `magick source.jpg -strip -colorspace sRGB -type TrueColor PNG24:source.png`. 2. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts prepare painted-steel source.png`: the last 128 columns and rows are cross-faded into the first ones (seamless, 896x896), the broad light and shade is removed (a wrapping box blur of radius 112 subtracted, the mean kept), and the image is area-averaged to 512x512, converted to grey (Rec. 709 luminance) with its mean moved to 224 of 255 so the renderer tint sets the colour. 3. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts derive` writes normal.png, roughness.png and metalness.png from basecolor.png. 4. 2026-11-24, after the owner's review of the pilot (the surface looked pitted at close range): the recipe of this material in tools/plant/textures.ts became heightBlur 4, normalStrength 0.08, roughness 0.95 to 0.88 (it was heightBlur 2, normalStrength 0.6, roughness 0.55 to 0.4), for a smooth, satin surface, and `bun tools/plant/textures.ts derive` wrote normal.png and roughness.png again; basecolor.png and metalness.png did not change. The roughness map is now a narrow band near 1 that the renderer's roughness of each surface scales.
